source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench: How ready are language model agents for oncall?
finding: Frontier coding agents are far from expert on-call diagnosis. Strict accuracy needs all root causes named.
numbers: Best RCA accuracy 25.3% on Medium tasks and 10.0% on Hard (5 agents, 1,079 tasks). Over 884 incident tasks the best strict accuracy was 30.9% (Claude Sonnet 4.6); best partial-credit depth 48.8% (GPT-5.5). Verified subset (32 tasks): Fable 5 depth 58.2+-5.8%, accuracy 40.6+-8.8%.
quote: agents are far from being intelligent SREs
limits: Simulated microservice testbed with public code (Astronomy Shop); standalone tasks. Real systems are larger.
agent_relevance: Baseline for how far a scaffold-free agent is from expert level; scaffold gains must be shown against this gap.

source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench: How ready are language model agents for oncall?
finding: Agents lock onto the loudest symptom and miss other root causes. This matches the novice habit of surface-feature focus.
numbers: Manual scoring of the Verified subset: one model was distracted by a persistent background issue and missed the active cause; another traced the chain correctly to the feature flag.
limits: Qualitative, from a hand-scored subset (32 tasks).
agent_relevance: S0 should force a check of ranked alternatives before committing; salience is not relevance.

source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench: How ready are language model agents for oncall?
finding: Access to the system source code (a model of the system) matters a lot for diagnosis quality.
numbers: Removing source code cut RCA accuracy by 9-16 points across models and raised hallucination for every model. Incident-time accuracy stayed robust (Opus 4.7: 82.6% to 79.9%).
limits: N=884 incident tasks; mean +-1 SE reported.
agent_relevance: Supports giving the agent an explicit model of the system, not only observations.

source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench: How ready are language model agents for oncall?
finding: Vaguer reports and later detection make diagnosis harder. Less input context is a large moderator.
numbers: Reducing input context dropped RCA accuracy by 19-50 points across models. The weakest model invented an implausible root cause in 40% of reports.
limits: Ablation on report specificity and time-to-detection.
agent_relevance: Agent should gather missing context first; invented causes need a falsification step.

source: Gong et al. (2026) ORCA-bench: How ready are language model agents for oncall?
finding: Agents waste tool calls on bad queries.
numbers: 26-40% of telemetry calls errored or returned empty.
limits: Rates read from the paper text; per-model detail in figure only.
agent_relevance: Cheap early checks that a probe can return data would save budget.

source: Clark et al. (2026) SREGym: a live benchmark for AI SRE agents
finding: Agents treat the first plausible anomaly as the target failure, so ambient noise hurts diagnosis. Mitigation is more robust than diagnosis.
numbers: Diagnosis success fell with noise for every agent-model pair. Claude Code (Sonnet 4.6) 72.6% to 62.6% diagnosis; Stratus (Sonnet 4.6) 61.5% to 51.5%, E2E 54.8% to 39.6%. Diagnosis range 38.1-72.6%.
quote: all the evaluated agents take a greedy approach
limits: 90 problems; noise = two patterns every 5 min, 2 min each. Table pairing of noise vs no-noise rows read from layout text.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence of an anchoring failure novices also show; supports S0 hypothesis-set discipline.

source: Clark et al. (2026) SREGym: a live benchmark for AI SRE agents
finding: Pattern-matching a known symptom to a fix often works without a correct diagnosis.
numbers: When initial diagnosis was wrong, mitigation still succeeded 22-62% of the time across agents. Stratus/Sonnet 4.6 needed 3.82 attempts after a wrong diagnosis vs 1.88 after a right one.
limits: Without noise injected.
agent_relevance: Matches rule-based expert behaviour (Rasmussen): symptom to action. Fast for known faults, risky for novel ones.

source: Clark et al. (2026) SREGym: a live benchmark for AI SRE agents
finding: Performance falls sharply on new failure types (metastable, correlated) compared with ported familiar ones.
numbers: E2E success fell from 63.7% to 17.9% (Stratus/Sonnet 4.6), 60.8% to 28.2% (Claude Code), 57.8% to 15.4% (Codex) on new scenarios.
limits: Difficulty is partly confounded with novelty.
agent_relevance: Looks like experience-bound schemas that do not transfer; memory should store causes, not only surface fixes.

source: Jha et al. (2025) ITBench: evaluating AI agents across real-world IT automation tasks
finding: Weak SRE results for 2024-era models on realistic scenarios; observability data is essential.
numbers: SRE scenarios resolved 13.8%; CISO 25.2%; FinOps 0%. GPT-4o best diagnosis pass@1 13.81%, mitigation 11.43%. Without traces: diagnosis 13.81% to 9.52%, mitigation to 2.86%.
limits: 94 scenarios (42 SRE); baseline agents; older models.
agent_relevance: Shows the cost of missing evidence; read with ORCA and SREGym for 2026 levels.

source: Tian et al. (2026) GALA: graph-augmented LLM agents for root cause analysis
finding: Bounding exploration with the service dependency graph (a structured model) beats free exploration and fixed procedures.
numbers: GALA+ 74.44% AC@1 on Online Boutique, 73.33% on Train Ticket. Best prior LLM method (Flow-of-Action) 48.35% and 47.78%. GraphRAG 21.35% and 7.78% AC@1 despite the most tokens.
limits: Two benchmarks plus AegisLab (100 cases). Authors' own method.
agent_relevance: A system model that constrains search is what experts have; suggests encoding it in the scaffold.

source: Tian et al. (2026) GALA: graph-augmented LLM agents for root cause analysis
finding: Single-modality or unconstrained LLM approaches fail through spurious signals and invented components.
numbers: BARO over-predicted Redis because of persistent disk spikes; mABC hallucinated non-existent service names. GALA+ fixed 27 incidents Flow-of-Action missed vs 4 reverse on OB (35 vs 12 on TT; p<0.001).
limits: One-sided exact binomial test.
agent_relevance: Same lure as noise: persistent but irrelevant signals.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Potential and limitations of LLMs for novice program fault localization
finding: 13 LLMs on novice-program fault localization; accuracy falls as difficulty rises. Reasoning models need little prompt design.
numbers: Codeflaws Top-1 at Lv5 vs Lv1: o3 44 vs 64; GPT-4 35 vs 65; GPT-3.5-Turbo 27 vs 55 (counts). o1-preview Condefects Top-5 57 (Lv5) to 86 (Lv1).
limits: New BugT set looked too easy (o1-mini and o1-preview both 89 Top-5 at Lv5).
agent_relevance: Difficulty gradient is a known moderator; GPT-4 relied on novice-style prompts, reasoning models did not.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Potential and limitations of LLMs for novice program fault localization
finding: Raters with 1 year of programming experience rated LLM fault explanations higher than raters with 3 years.
numbers: One-year group gave higher ratings on all five dimensions; three-year group discriminated more between model types.
limits: Small questionnaire; sample size not recorded from the parts read.
agent_relevance: Novice judges are less able to spot weak explanations: do not use novice-like checks as the only verifier.

source: Xu et al. (2025) Potential and limitations of LLMs for novice program fault localization
finding: Bigger or newer is not always better, and over-reasoning hurts clarity.
numbers: o1 sometimes underperformed GPT-3.5-Turbo; some models gave excessive explanation that hid the fault line. Different methods found different faults.
limits: Single study; models of 2023-2025.
agent_relevance: Cross-checking with different methods adds coverage.

source: Ma, Shen, Koedinger, Wu (2023/2024) HypoCompass: LLMs as teachable agent for debugging
finding: Having novices hypothesise causes while an LLM does adjacent work improved novice debugging.
numbers: N=19 students. Pre- to post-test score +11.7% (paired t, p=0.033); time -13.6% (p=0.003). Hypothesis completeness: score +6.1%, time -23.6%; accuracy: score +15.8%, time -9.0%. Pre-test means 54% (LO1) vs 38% (LO2).
limits: Tiny sample, no control group, one hour; gains confounded with item difficulty.
agent_relevance: Training the hypothesis step is the active ingredient; matches the expert-novice gap in hypothesis quality.

source: Ma, Shen, Koedinger, Wu (2023/2024) HypoCompass: LLMs as teachable agent for debugging
finding: LLM produced training bugs and fixes faster than a human teaching assistant.
numbers: Reported as about fourfold more efficient than human counterparts; quality rated high.
limits: Authors' own rating; small evaluation.
agent_relevance: LLMs can generate varied faults for practice and case memory.

source: Englhardt et al. (2023) LLMs for embedded system development and debugging
finding: A structured human-AI workflow helped novices most in hardware debugging.
numbers: N=15 users. Mean score with GPT plus workflow 65.48 vs 34.21 with no GPT (t(38)=2.73, p<0.01). Sensor task success 25% to 100%, including users with no hardware experience. GPT-4 perfect end-to-end on hardest tasks 14% (N=50).
limits: Five per condition; students and staff; GPT-4 era.
agent_relevance: Expert knowledge delivered as a procedure narrowed the novice gap; supports a scaffold for the agent.

source: Englhardt et al. (2023) LLMs for embedded system development and debugging
finding: Domain facts are a main failure: models hallucinate hardware details that experts know.
numbers: On one sensor task a model got the I2C address wrong from a pin voltage 38% of the time and hallucinated a register value 100% of the time; GPT-4 found the address 96% and produced working code 16%.
limits: Task-specific; one sensor task.
agent_relevance: Retrieve verified facts before reasoning about unfamiliar parts.
